Jagdish: so basically everyone said my speech was "so perfect" today
Preeti: it was good!! you should be proud 😊
Jagdish: thanks. but Rohit said it and his smile looked kind of stiff
Preeti: stiff how
Jagdish: like he was smiling with his teeth only. And Nina keeps saying she's my best friend but she never sat with me before the election
Preeti: hmm. maybe some of it's real and some isn't
Jagdish: yeah. I don't want to get paranoid though
Preeti: you don't have to. Just stay kind to everyone and keep the people who were there before. Like me 😄
Jagdish: obviously you're in the inner circle

qa.q: What did everyone say about Jagdish's speech?
What is Jagdish sensing behind the compliments, and how does Jagdish feel about it?
qa.a: Jagdish suspects some envy, as Rohit's smile looked stiff and Nina only got close after the election, but doesn't want to get paranoid.

qa.q: What would you advise Jagdish to do about his popularity?
qa.a: Stay kind and honest with everyone, not assume every compliment is friendship or envy, and keep a few real friends close.

qa.q: How might Rohit see Jagdish's speech?
qa.a: Possibly with mixed feelings. His stiff smile might mean envy, but Jagdish can't be sure, and it could just be his own shyness.

grounding: A popular student senses envy behind compliments and stays kind while keeping close a few real friends.

passage:
It was student council election day, and the whole school was buzzing. Nikita had been class favourite for three years: good at debate, captain of the netball team, always surrounded.
Uma found her in the corridor ten minutes before the results. "You'll win, obviously. You always win everything, na?" She smiled, but her eyes didn't.
Nikita felt the little sting in it. Lately there were a lot of compliments like that, sweet on top, sour underneath.
The results came: Nikita won by six votes. A crowd rushed around her. Uma clapped from the edge.
For a moment Nikita wanted to say something sharp back, to remind everyone who was on top. She didn't.
She walked over to Uma. "You gave the best speech today," she said honestly. "Your point about the library was better than mine."
Then she found her oldest friends, Tara and Sahana, who had been quietly waiting by the stairs. Those were the ones she hugged.

qa.q: By how many votes did Nikita win?
What was Nikita feeling when Uma complimented her?
qa.a: She sensed envy, feeling a little sting in a compliment that was sweet on top and sour underneath.

qa.q: Which choices kept Nikita kind and grounded?
qa.a: She resisted a sharp reply, praised Uma's speech honestly, and went to her oldest, real friends rather than the crowd.

qa.q: How might Uma feel when Nikita praises her speech?
qa.a: Uma may feel surprised and disarmed, and perhaps a little less envious, because the praise was honest.

grounding: A popular teen senses envy behind compliments, stays kind and honest, and keeps a few real friends close.

passage:
Gurpreet had become popular almost overnight after her dance video at the school fest in their Chandigarh school. Suddenly everyone wanted to sit with her.
Binita, from the next section, was one of them. "Wow, your hair is always perfect," she said. "Must be nice when everything just comes easy." The others laughed.
Gurpreet smiled, but on the bus home she felt uneasy. Binita had never talked to her before the fest. And "comes easy" hurt: she practised two hours every day.
She thought about who had been there in Class 7, when nobody knew her name. Only Jasmeet, who still sat with her at lunch, and Harman from the bus.
The next day, when Binita said, "You're so lucky," Gurpreet said gently, "Honestly, I practise a lot. It isn't luck." No sarcasm, no put-down.
At lunch, she sat with Jasmeet and Harman, like always. The crowd could come or go.

qa.q: What made Gurpreet popular almost overnight?
qa.a: Her dance video at the school fest.

qa.q: How did Gurpreet feel on the bus home?
qa.a: She felt uneasy and a bit hurt, sensing envy behind Binita's compliment and the suggestion that things came easy.

qa.q: What did Gurpreet do that was wise?
qa.a: She replied honestly and gently without a put-down, and stayed close to the real friends who had been there before.

qa.q: How might Binita see Gurpreet's popularity?
qa.a: Binita seems envious, thinking Gurpreet's success is luck, not seeing the hours of practice behind it.

grounding: A popular teen senses envy behind compliments, answers honestly without cruelty and stays close to real friends.
